say: You give it formula 4, $\cos(A-B)=\cos A\cos B+\sin A\sin B$. It builds a new formula from it, $\sin(A+B)$, and shows where it comes from.
The key idea is that a sine is a cosine of the **complement**: $\sin\theta=\cos(90^\circ-\theta)$. Turn the sine into a cosine, then use formula 4.

how.higher: On Paper 2 it came up once, in 2023, as a 10-mark part of its own: derive $\sin(A+B)$, then use it to find an exact value such as $\sin 75^\circ$.

example.question: Using $\cos(A-B)=\cos A\cos B+\sin A\sin B$, show that $\sin(A-B)=\sin A\cos B-\cos A\sin B$.

steps.title: Turn sine into cosine
steps.say: A sine is the cosine of the complement. Write $\sin(A-B)$ as $\cos\big(90^\circ-(A-B)\big)$, then move the brackets so it looks like $\cos(X-Y)$.

steps.title: Use formula 4
steps.say: This has the shape $\cos(X-Y)$ with $X=\hl{1}{90^\circ-A}$ and $Y=\hl{2}{-B}$. Write out formula 4 with those two angles.

steps.title: Simplify each factor
steps.say: Use $\cos(90^\circ-A)=\sin A$ and $\sin(90^\circ-A)=\cos A$. Cosine is even and sine is odd, so $\cos(-B)=\cos B$ and $\sin(-B)=-\sin B$.

higher.tip: Do not rely on trying numbers. Checking the formula for one pair of angles earns only low partial credit, so derive it for general $A$ and $B$.

say: You give it formula 5, $\cos(A+B)=\cos A\cos B-\sin A\sin B$. It gives back a formula for the **double angle**, $\cos 2A$.
The key idea is that $2A$ is just $A+A$. Put $B=A$ into formula 5 and tidy up.

how.higher: On Paper 2 it came up in 2021, as a 10-mark part of its own: show that $\cos 2A=\cos^2 A-\sin^2 A$, then use the result to find $\cos\theta$ from a given value of $\sin\frac{\theta}{2}$.

example.question: Using $\cos(A+B)=\cos A\cos B-\sin A\sin B$, show that $\cos 2A=2\cos^2 A-1$.

steps.title: Make the angle a sum
steps.say: $2A$ is $A+A$. Write $\cos 2A$ as $\cos(A+A)$ so formula 5 applies, with $B=A$.

steps.title: Use formula 5
steps.say: Put $B=A$ into formula 5. Every $B$ becomes an $A$.

steps.title: Remove the sine
steps.say: The target has only cosines. Replace $\hl{2}{\sin^2 A}$ with $1-\cos^2 A$, since $\sin^2 A+\cos^2 A=1$.

higher.tip: Show the substitution. Writing $\cos(A+A)$ with $B=A$ put in is high partial credit, so do not jump to the answer.
Testing the formula with a value of $A$ earns only low partial credit. Derive it for a general $A$.

say: You give it formulae 5 and 7, the expansions of $\cos(A+B)$ and $\sin(A+B)$. It gives back a formula for $\tan(A+B)$ in terms of $\tan A$ and $\tan B$.
The key idea is $\tan\theta=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$. Write $\tan(A+B)$ as a fraction, expand top and bottom, then divide every term by $\cos A\cos B$.

example.question: Using $\sin(A+B)=\sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B$ and $\cos(A+B)=\cos A\cos B-\sin A\sin B$, show that $\tan 2A=\dfrac{2\tan A}{1-\tan^2 A}$.

steps.title: Write tan as a fraction
steps.say: Tangent is sine over cosine, and $2A=A+A$. Write $\tan 2A$ as $\dfrac{\sin(A+A)}{\cos(A+A)}$.

steps.title: Expand top and bottom
steps.say: Use formula 7 on the top and formula 5 on the bottom, with $B=A$.

lines.tex: &= \frac{\sin A\cos A+\cos A\sin A}{\cos A\cos A-\sin A\sin A}

steps.title: Divide by cos squared A
steps.say: The answer has only tangents. Divide the top and the bottom by $\hl{1}{\cos^2 A}$, so that each $\dfrac{\sin A}{\cos A}$ becomes $\tan A$.

lines.tex: &= \frac{\dfrac{2\sin A\cos A}{\hl{1}{\cos^2 A}}}{\dfrac{\cos^2 A}{\hl{1}{\cos^2 A}}-\dfrac{\sin^2 A}{\hl{1}{\cos^2 A}}}

say: You give it a right-angled triangle with an angle and a side, or two sides. It finds a **missing side** or a missing angle.
Name the sides from the angle you are using: opposite, adjacent, hypotenuse. Then pick the ratio, sine, cosine or tangent, that uses the two sides you are working with.

how.higher: On Paper 2 it is a step inside bigger Section B questions on circles, bearings and real settings, worth 5 to 10 marks a part, and it came up in every year from 2015 to 2025.
how.ordinary: On Paper 2 it is a part of its own, 5 to 10 marks, in most years from 2015 to 2025, usually in a real setting such as a ladder, a ramp or a slope.

example.question: A ladder 6 m long leans against a vertical wall. The foot of the ladder is 2 m from the wall. Find the angle the ladder makes with the ground. Give your answer correct to one decimal place.

steps.title: Name the sides
steps.say: The angle $A$ is at the foot of the ladder. The ladder is the **hypotenuse**, and the 2 m along the ground is **adjacent** to $A$.

steps.title: Choose the ratio
steps.say: Adjacent and hypotenuse go together in **cosine**. Write the ratio and put in the numbers.

steps.title: Find the angle
steps.say: Use inverse cosine to get the angle from its cosine. Make sure the calculator is in degree mode.
